stem: A nurse plans care for a client whose cultural background differs from the nurse’s. Which action best reflects culturally responsive nursing care?

options.A: Use a standardized cultural profile to predict preferences instead of asking the individual client about values or practices.
options.B: Exclude cultural practices from the plan whenever biomedical treatment is available, even when the practices are safe.
options.C: Avoid discussing culture or health beliefs so cultural differences cannot influence communication or care planning.
options.D: Ask about the individual client’s cultural values, health beliefs, and preferences and incorporate relevant practices when compatible with safe, effective care.

rationale: HHS National CLAS Standard 1 calls for effective, understandable, respectful care and services responsive to cultural health beliefs and practices, languages, health literacy, and communication needs. HHS also describes CLAS as respecting the whole individual and responding to the individual's health needs and preferences. D is therefore the culturally responsive approach.
educational_objective: Provide culturally responsive care by eliciting the individual client's beliefs, practices, and preferences rather than stereotyping, and integrate relevant preferences into safe care planning.
source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Minority Health
source_document_title: National Standards for Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services (CLAS) in Health and Health Care
source_version_date: Current National CLAS Standards; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Principal Standard 1: provide effective, understandable and respectful quality care/services responsive to cultural health beliefs and practices, languages, health literacy and communication needs. What is CLAS?: respect the whole individual and respond to the individual's health needs and preferences.
source_claim_supported: Culturally responsive care should be respectful of and responsive to the individual client's cultural health beliefs, practices, communication needs and preferences rather than relying on stereotypes.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity: incorporate client cultural practices and beliefs when planning and providing care; use therapeutic communication and support psychosocial needs.
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — cultural beliefs/practices and individualized care

source_original.stem: A nurse plans care for a client whose cultural background differs from the nurse’s. Which action best reflects culturally responsive nursing care?

options.A: Use a standardized cultural profile to predict preferences instead of asking the individual client about values or practices.
options.B: Exclude cultural practices from the plan whenever biomedical treatment is available, even when the practices are safe.
options.C: Avoid discussing culture or health beliefs so cultural differences cannot influence communication or care planning.
options.D: Ask about the individual client’s cultural values and practices and incorporate relevant preferences when compatible with safe, effective care.

source_original.rationale: HHS CLAS standards call for respectful care responsive to cultural health beliefs and practices; the NCSBN Psychosocial Integrity blueprint specifically includes incorporating client cultural practices and beliefs when planning and providing care.
source_original.source_detail: Principal Standard 1 — care responsive to cultural health beliefs and practices, languages, health literacy and communication needs. National CLAS Standards currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10: cultural practices/beliefs, grief/loss, therapeutic communication and mental-health issues. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained key D, made the individual-preference assessment explicit, anchored the item to HHS CLAS Standard 1, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because it tests a direct culturally responsive-care principle.

audit_findings.source_authority: HHS Office of Minority Health National CLAS Standards; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: National CLAS Principal Standard 1 and HHS What is CLAS page
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item emphasizes individualized elicitation of beliefs/preferences and avoids stereotyping or automatic exclusion of safe cultural practices.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because a profile cannot replace asking the individual about preferences.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because compatible cultural practices need not be excluded merely because biomedical treatment exists.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because respectful assessment of beliefs and communication needs is part of responsive care.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D is individualized, respectful, responsive and safety-compatible.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe approaches to cultural differences; D is keyed by content, not wording form.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity — cultural practices/beliefs in care planning.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read HHS CLAS Standard 1 and NCSBN mapping, all options, rationale and objective. D remained uniquely correct.
